exposure: Clinical variables (gender, age at diagnosis, gestational maturity, birth weight, perinatal complications, comorbid symptoms, hereditary background, neuromuscular function, epilepsy, neuroimaging, electroencephalography patterns)
outcome: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic single nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions
Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic copy number variations
cohort: The study included 115 children aged 1 month to 16 years with unexplained developmental delay or intellectual disability (DD/ID) who underwent whole-genome sequencing.
finding: Whole-genome sequencing identified diagnostic genetic variants in 22 (19%) of 115 pediatric patients with unexplained DD/ID, and an earlier age at diagnosis was significantly associated with an increased diagnostic yield.
